basis: Congenital renal calyceal malformation; urinary infections and stones are separately diagnosed complications.
Defining neurodevelopmental disorder; hypodontia affects 3/7 patients. Hearing impairment in 2/7 is below 30%.
Chronic destructive atrophy of nasal mucosa; the nasal airway belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Myofibrillar protein defects cause structural skeletal myopathy; cardiac involvement varies by subtype and is not established as common across this umbrella.
Y. pestis infection; skin ulcers and destructive blistering are frequent (30-79%). Pneumonia is occasional; hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish dysfunction.
Malignant neoplasm of the tonsil, a pharyngeal structure. Lymphoma is only one subtype and does not define this umbrella.
Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; intellectual disability 5/6, muscle weakness 2/5 with myopathic fibers 2/3, and optic atrophy 2/6 support involvement.
Clonal plasma-cell light-chain deposition disorder; renal involvement ~60-70% and cardiac ~50-70%. Neuropathy and hepatic dysfunction are generally below 30%.
Benign or malignant neoplasm involving the stomach.
Corpus callosum agenesis and ocular coloboma define the syndrome; amenorrhea alone does not establish endocrine disease.
Neoplasm localized to the tonsil, within the pharyngeal airway.
Colorectal cancer susceptibility defines this hereditary syndrome; associated cancers are separately diagnosed risks, not direct additional organ involvement.
Ependymal CNS tumor, often supratentorial.
Angiosarcoma localized to the gallbladder; vascular histology does not establish additional cardiovascular disease.
Parainfluenza type 4 causes respiratory tract infection.
Defective regulation of complement/kinin mediators produces hypersensitivity, angioedema and chronic urticaria; common pulmonary damage is not established.
Neuronal migration malformation; associated skull/ethmoid bone defects and encephaloceles are frequent (30-79%) in supplied phenotypes.
Defining malformations affect external ears, mouth (microstomia), and hypopharynx (papillomata); evidence is limited to one patient or family.
Recurrent respiratory infections and malabsorption define disease; progressive renal failure in both reported sibs. Cataracts and otitis omitted because of the cap.
Histologic category without an explicit site; gastric origin is supported by the representative example and sole listed child.
Defining albinism, intestinal aganglionosis and deafness; polycythemia reported in 1/1 patient. Fundus hypopigmentation lacks documented visual dysfunction.
Self-limited papulosquamous skin disease; an infectious or autoimmune mechanism is not sufficiently established for an additional mechanism label.
Inherited ferritin-regulation disorder with early cataracts; hyperferritinemia occurs without iron overload or demonstrated liver or blood-cell damage.
Neonatal aspiration disease directly injures the lungs.
Skeletal dysplasia; night blindness and gingival overgrowth are very frequent (80-99%). Ear shape and hirsutism lack documented functional damage.
